text:
Maya: Heads-up — need final alignment on the composable add-ons proposal before Acme's sales demo tomorrow. Quick thread to agree scope and launch gates.
Adrian: Got it. What's Acme specifically asking for?
Sam (sales): They want a per-route throughput addon + a priority lane. They only commit to mid-tier otherwise. Their ask: mix-and-match addons per contract so they can buy priority only for a subset of routes.
Sophia: That triggers metering changes. Our current quota/billing model is org-wide (per-tenant). Per-route entitlements will need tagging and new aggregation in billing.
Jeff: Also decision on hardcap vs softcap for addons. Acme explicitly requested a hardcap (block after limit). Hardcap gives predictability but has UX/support cost; softcap allows overage billing.
Maya: Tradeoffs noted. Hardcap simplifies capacity guarantees (helps SLA) but increases support surface and risks production interruptions for customers if misconfigured.
Adrian: Proposed compromise: enable hardcap only as an enterprise toggle (contract opt-in). Mid-tier/plg gets only softcap. That reduces risk and keeps product simpler for most customers.
Sam (sales): Legal will likely push back on heavy SLA credits. They also asked if seat-based discounts can apply when purchasing the priority lane addon — they want a blended price.
Sophia: Implementation notes: billing pipeline change + console UI to select per-route addons + enforcement on router. Rough estimate: infra 2 sprints, frontend 1 sprint, billing validation 1 sprint. Need pricing review.
Maya: Pilot suggestion: run pilot with Acme + one reference customer, restrict pilot to Dedicated and Private deployments (so we can control capacity).
Jeff: Draft launch criteria: 
- billing support for per-route metering and invoice line-items
- UI for addon selection and visibility per-route
- enforcement + graceful fallback policy (softcap fallback or queued requests)
- telemetry showing per-route token distribution and overage events
If any of these fail in pilot, fallback to offering only softcap.
Maya: Quick sample SKU mapping for review:
```
addons: {
  "priority_lane": { "sku": "ADD-PRIORITY-01", "meter": "priority_tokens" },
  "route_throughput": { "sku": "ADD-ROUTE-THR-01", "meter": "route_tokens" }
}
```
Adrian: That SKU model works. We should include a contract clause template for hardcap opt-in and overage handling.
pricing-bot: Reminder: pricing changes require legal signoff and an ARR uplift check. Also mark this for the next pricing review board.
Sam (sales): I'll draft the Acme contract language and loop in Legal + Solutions Eng. Planning to propose hardcap opt-in with a mitigated SLA credit formula. :thumbsup:
Adrian: I'll schedule an infra sync and slot the work for next sprint if Product prioritizes.
Sophia: 6-week ETA for pilot readiness if we start this sprint (assuming no scope creep).
Maya: Thanks all. I pushed an initial spec to internal docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/pricing/composable-addons-draft — review by EOD so we can finalize before the demo. /remind me 24h before demo
